steps.question: Do the 12 adipose samples (6 treated vs 6 control) show any batch-like structure, outliers, or a confound with sex or age before fitting the DE model?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances colored by condition/batch per R-0033; strandedness-unknown flagged per R-0079 as a caveat since only counts (no alignments) are available to re-infer it.

steps.description: Load counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples) and metadata.csv (condition, sex, age per sample). Apply DESeq2's blind variance-stabilizing transform, compute PCA on the top 500 most variable genes, and draw a sample-distance heatmap. Color/label PCA and heatmap by condition, by sex, and by age (continuous). Report library sizes per sample. steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test adjusted for sex and age (treated vs control)
steps.question: Which genes differ between treated and control adipose samples after adjusting for sex and age?

grounding.reason: Covariates (sex, age) enter the design as fixed effects per R-0023; explicit reference level per R-0036; DESeq2 Wald + apeglm is the primary method with edgeR QLF as the required robustness cross-check at n=6/group per R-0001/R-0042; BH+independent filtering at alpha 0.05 per R-0010.

steps.description: Pre-filter genes to those with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size). Build a DESeqDataSet with design = ~ sex + age_centered + condition, where age is centered (mean-subtracted) before the fit and condition is an explicit factor with 'control' set as the reference level. Do not regress covariates out of counts beforehand — they enter the model as fixed-effect terms. Use DESeq2's internal median-of-ratios normalization (no pre-normalization of counts). Run the Wald test on the condition_treated_vs_control coefficient. Keep DESeq2's default count-outlier handling (Cook's distance NA-flagging with 6 replicates/group). Apply apeglm shrinkage to the condition coefficient for the reported log2 fold change, keeping the unshrunken estimate and its SE alongside it. Adjust p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg with independent filtering on, alpha=0.05. Inspect and report the raw p-value histogram shape before trusting the adjustment. Separately, fit an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the identical design matrix (~ sex + age_centered + condition) as a robustness cross-check; report the number of significant genes (padj<0.05) from each tool and the size of their intersection as the high-confidence gene set, with tool-specific-only genes reported as a secondary set.
acceptance_criteria: Design formula ~ sex + age_centered + condition used, with condition reference level = control stated explicitly
DESeq2 Wald test results table has unshrunken log2FC, apeglm-shrunken log2FC, lfcSE, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value columns
Number of genes tested after filtering, number with padj<0.05, and number of NA p-values from outlier flagging are reported
p-value histogram inspected and its shape reported
edgeR QLF test run on the same design; DESeq2/edgeR significant-gene overlap and per-tool-only gene counts reported
MA plot and dispersion plot included as fit diagnostics

steps.name: Functional enrichment of the treated-vs-control gene signature
steps.question: Which biological pathways or processes are over-represented among the genes that differ between treated and control adipose samples?

grounding.reason: The knowledge check (execute_knowledge_check) rejected preranked fgsea as the default enrichment method for this exact situation profile and named over-representation analysis with an explicit universe as the permitted method (rule R-0048/violation surfaced against fgsea). The step is therefore drafted primarily as ORA per that finding, with fgsea retained only as the documented fallback per rule R-0103 (few significant genes -> ORA has no power, use ranked method), since which regime applies depends on the DE result size that is not yet known at planning time.

steps.description: Map gene symbols from the DESeq2 results table to Entrez IDs using org.Hs.eg.db (report the unmapped share). If the number of genes with padj<0.05 is at least ~50, run over-representation analysis (clusterProfiler::enricher) of that significant gene list against three pathway collections available in the reference store: MSigDB Hallmark (human, 2026.1), Reactome (current release GMT), and WikiPathways human (2026.07.10 snapshot) — run each collection separately (never merged into one set list) with an explicit universe restricted to all genes that passed the low-count filter and were tested (not the whole genome), a gene-set size window of 15-500 members after intersecting with the universe, and BH adjustment within each collection. If fewer than ~50 genes reach padj<0.05, fall back to preranked fgsea on the full list of tested genes ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic against the same three collections, and state in the report that this fallback was triggered along with the count of significant genes. State the exact contrast (treated vs control, reference=control) and its sign convention, the release of each gene-set collection, and collapse redundant significant sets before reporting, keeping the full table as a supplement. List leading-edge / core-enrichment genes for each significant set.
acceptance_criteria: Gene ID mapping to Entrez performed with org.Hs.eg.db, unmapped share reported
Enrichment method choice (ORA vs preranked fgsea) stated along with the number of significant DE genes that determined the choice
Each of Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways run and reported separately with its release/version stated
Universe explicitly stated as the tested genes, not the whole genome
Gene sets restricted to 15-500 members after intersecting with the universe
Redundant significant sets collapsed with one representative reported and full table kept as supplement
Leading-edge/core genes listed per significant set

plan.title: Adipose treated vs control DE adjusted for sex and age
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human adipose-tissue samples (6 treated, 6 control), unpaired, single batch, salmon-derived gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples after dropping the gene-symbol column), with sex and age recorded per sample and the groups NOT matched on age. Because sex and age can confound a treated-vs-control comparison in adipose tissue (both are known drivers of adipose gene expression), the design must adjust for them rather than test condition alone or regress them out beforehand (the latter is flagged by the knowledge base as inflating false confidence in an unbalanced design). The plan therefore: (1) profiles sample structure with a blind variance-stabilizing transform, PCA and a sample-distance heatmap, colored by condition, sex, and age, to check for confounding structure and outliers before any test is fit; (2) fits DESeq2 with design ~ sex + age_centered + condition (explicit reference level = control), a minimal low-count pre-filter, median-of-ratios normalization internal to DESeq2, a Wald test on the condition coefficient, apeglm shrinkage of the log2 fold change, and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment with independent filtering at alpha 0.05 — this isolates the treatment effect controlling for the two known covariates; (3) runs edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same design as a robustness cross-check and reports the overlap of the two significant gene sets as the high-confidence result, per the knowledge base's replicate-count guidance (6 per group falls in the 2-11 range where both tools are recommended and cross-checked); (4) runs functional enrichment on the full ranked gene list (all tested genes ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic) using fgsea against MSigDB Hallmark (human, 2026.1) as the first pass, then Reactome and WikiPathways as follow-up collections, all present in the reference store; (5) produces a single report bundling QC diagnostics, the DE gene table (unshrunken and shrunken log2FC, unadjusted and adjusted p-values), the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, the enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and a full reproducibility record (package versions, seed, collection versions). The knowledge-check flagged that fgsea (ranked) is not the base-recommended enrichment method for this exact situation profile and that an over-representation analysis with an explicit universe is preferred instead; given the DE step is expected to yield a workable number of significant genes at n=6/group with two covariates, the enrichment step is planned as ORA (clusterProfiler enricher, universe = tested genes) against Hallmark/Reactome/WikiPathways, with a documented fallback to preranked fgsea on the full list only if fewer than ~50 genes reach significance (per rule R-0103), since a hypergeometric test on a very short list has no power. Strandedness is unknown from the profile; the QC step will note this data limitation but cannot re-run alignment since only counts are supplied, so it inherits whatever strand setting Salmon used and this is documented as a limitation rather than fixed.

design = ~ sex + age_centered + condition, reference level condition=control
apeglm shrinkage on the condition coefficient

DE + enrichment report with diagnostics, reproducibility record
design = ~ sex + age_centered + condition, explicit reference level set for condition (control)
fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark human then Reactome and WikiPathways
